title: The Cop and the Anthem
summary: A homeless man tries to get arrested for the winter, but his plans keep failing.

sentences.text: On a cold autumn night, an old man named Soapy sat on a stone seat in a public park.
Winter was coming fast, and he needed a warm place to stay during the freezing months ahead.
His plan was simple and clear.
He wanted to be arrested so that he could spend the season in a comfortable prison with free food.
He knew that the city jail would provide him protection against the bad weather.
The man hoped that his simple scheme would work immediately.
He walked away from the park and looked around the streets.
Every year, many people faced similar problems when the cold season arrived.
Soapy wanted to make sure that he would not suffer during the dark nights.
He knew that the police would keep him safe if he broke a small rule.
Therefore, the old man prepared himself for the next part of his plan.
He walked slowly through the cold air while he thought about his future in the jail.
Soapy stood up and walked into a bright restaurant on a famous street.
He ate a large meal without any money, and then he calmly told the waiter that he could not pay.
However, the manager did not call the police.
Instead, the workers simply threw him out onto the cold ground.
His first small scheme had failed completely, but he did not give up yet.
He stood on the stone street and thought about what he should do next.
The bright lights of the restaurant made him feel even more tired.
Many customers looked at him with strange expressions.
The manager told the staff to ignore the poor man.
Soapy realized that he needed a different approach to solve his problem.
He walked away from the building and started to look for another opportunity.
He hoped that his next attempt would bring better results.
Next, Soapy tried to break a big glass window in front of a store using a heavy rock.
An officer came running over quickly, but the man thought that Soapy was just a happy customer who had made a mistake.
The person tried another silly trick near a theater, shouting loudly and acting like a crazy person.
Again, no police officer would arrest him, because they believed that university students were only playing games.
Soapy felt very sad and upset by these strange failures.
He wondered why the officers refused to take him away.
The heavy rock was still in his hand, but he dropped it on the ground.
People walked past him without paying any attention to his loud shouts.
He felt that the whole world was working against his simple plan.
The theater lights shone brightly above the street.
He left the area and continued his journey through the town.
After several strange and difficult attempts, Soapy felt very tired and walked away from the busy lights of the town.
He reached a quiet street where a beautiful old church stood against the dark sky.
Wonderful church music flowed out through the open door, and the sweet sound touched his heart deeply.
He looked at his past life and realized that he had wasted many years.
The sweet song reminded him of the days when his life was different.
He remembered his mother and the home where he grew up as a child.
Those memories made him feel a strong emotion inside his chest.
The music continued to play softly through the night air.
He stood very still and listened to every single note.
His mind changed as he thought about his future.
He decided that he would leave his bad habits behind.
Standing there in the quiet night, Soapy made a strong promise to change and find honest work tomorrow.
He decided that he would become a new person and build a better future for himself.
At that very moment, strangely, an officer put a heavy hand upon his shoulder.
The officer finally arrested him for standing around.
Soapy was sent to jail for three months.
The judge decided that the man must stay in the prison for the entire season.
Soapy accepted his sentence with a quiet mind.
He knew that his new life would start after he left the jail.
The cold winter would no longer trouble him inside the comfortable prison walls.
He felt that everything happened for a reason.
His long journey of change had finally begun.

sentences.text: On a biting autumn night, when dead leaves whispered across the asphalt like restless ghosts, an old man named Soapy sat upon a curved stone seat in Madison Square.
Winter was approaching with an unyielding swiftness, and the bitter air demanded a refuge for the freezing months that lay ahead.
His plan was deceptively simple, born of necessity and quiet desperation.
He wanted nothing more than to be arrested, trusting that the city jail would provide him with dependable shelter, three meals a day, and protection from the frost.
Every year, as the temperature plunged, countless destitute souls faced this very same dilemma, seeking a sanctuary behind iron bars.
Soapy preferred the stone walls of a prison cell over the charity of missions, which always demanded a degrading moral accounting in exchange for a cot.
Determined to execute his simple scheme, Soapy stood up from the cold bench and walked out of the park into the bustling stream of the avenue.
He made his way toward a brightly illuminated restaurant on Broadway, a famous street where wealthy diners gathered to escape the autumn chill.
The establishment was known for its lavish cuisine, catering to patrons who never worried about the cost of a single meal.
Soapy felt entirely confident that his worn coat and frayed trousers would invite suspicion the moment he crossed the threshold.
He stepped through the heavy glass doors, enveloped by the rich aroma of roasted meats and expensive wine, and walked straight to a table near the window.
Without hesitation, he ordered a large, expensive meal, planning to consume every morsel before revealing his penniless state to the management.
With deliberate slowness, Soapy ate every bite of the feast, savoring the food while his mind calculated the inevitable confrontation with the staff.
When the plates were finally empty, he looked up at the head waiter with a calm expression and stated quite plainly that he had not a single penny in his pockets.
He invited the man to call for an officer of the law without delay.
Yet, to Soapy s profound astonishment, the manager did not summon the police to escort him away in chains.
Instead, two large waiters silently seized him by his collar and the seat of his trousers, lifting him effortlessly off the ground.
They unceremoniously threw him out onto the cold stone pavement, leaving him to nurse his bruises in the gutter.
Stunned and humiliated, Soapy stood on the dark sidewalk and tried to formulate a new approach to his persistent problem.
The bright lights of the restaurant only served to emphasize his exhaustion and his miserable failure.
Passing customers glanced down at him with strange, pitying expressions, while the manager instructed the staff to ignore the poor wanderer entirely.
Soapy realized that the law treated him with a frustrating indifference, refusing to acknowledge his deliberate provocation.
He brushed the dust from his thin coat and walked away from the building, determined to find another opportunity to secure his winter lodging.
His first scheme had collapsed completely, but he refused to abandon his quest for a warm prison cell.
A few blocks away, Soapy noticed a large plate-glass window shining brilliantly in front of a prominent luxury store.
Seizing a heavy paving stone from the gutter, he crept toward the glass with a sudden burst of aggressive energy.
He hurled the stone directly at the window, expecting the shattering crash to bring a frantic police officer running instantly.
The glass broke with a loud, satisfying explosion that echoed sharply down the quiet street.
Moments later, a policeman came running over quickly, his heavy boots clattering against the pavement.
However, the officer took one look at Soapy s calm face and immediately concluded that the man was merely a merry customer who had made a foolish mistake.
Furious that his second attempt had failed, Soapy spotted a crowded theater district where people were laughing and talking loudly.
He decided to try another silly trick near the box office, shouting nonsense at the top of his lungs and acting like a raving lunatic.
He danced, he yelled, and he waved his arms wildly in the air, creating a chaotic scene in front of the startled ticket buyers.
Yet, once again, no police officer would arrest him for his bizarre public disturbance.
The local authorities simply believed that lively university students were only playing harmless games before the evening show.
Soapy felt deeply defeated by this infuriating display of leniency from the men in uniform.
He dropped the heavy rock from his tired hand and watched it roll silently into the gutter.
People walked past him without paying the slightest attention to his angry shouts or his pathetic appearance.
He felt as though the entire world was conspiring against his simple, practical plan.
The theater lights shone brilliantly above the street, casting long, mocking shadows across the pavement.
With a heavy heart, he left the busy area and continued his lonely journey through the labyrinth of the town.
The night grew colder, and his bones ached with a fatigue that went far beyond mere physical tiredness.
After several strange and difficult attempts, Soapy found himself walking away from the bright lights and the noisy crowds of the commercial district.
He reached a quiet, residential street where a beautiful old stone church stood proudly against the dark winter sky.
Wonderful, swelling organ music flowed out through the wide-open door into the crisp night air.
The sweet, melancholic sound touched his weary heart deeply, arresting his steps and demanding his full attention.
He looked back upon his wasted past life and realized with sudden clarity how many precious years he had thrown away.
The sacred song reminded him of a time when his existence was guided by different principles and higher hopes.
He remembered his mother, the peaceful countryside, and the modest home where he had grown up as an innocent child.
Those long-forgotten memories stirred a powerful emotion within his chest, bringing a rare moisture to his tired eyes.
The gentle music continued to play softly through the night, creating a bridge between his present misery and his vanished youth.
He stood very still in the shadow of the stone wall, listening intently to every single rising and falling note.
A profound mental shift occurred within his mind as he contemplated the bleak reality of his future.
He made a quiet resolution that he would finally leave his bad habits behind and redeem his broken life.
Standing there in the quiet night, Soapy made a firm, unshakeable promise to change his ways and find honest work the very next morning.
He decided that he would become a completely new person and build a respectable future through his own genuine effort.
He felt a sudden surge of optimism, believing that it was not too late to reclaim his dignity.
At that very moment, strangely, a heavy hand descended firmly upon his shoulder.
He turned around to see a stern police officer looking down at him with an expression of official authority.
The officer finally decided to arrest him simply for loitering idly on the sidewalk.
Soapy was promptly marched down to the local station house and formally charged before the magistrate the following morning.
The judge listened to the brief report and decided without hesitation that the man must stay in prison for the entire three-month winter season.
Soapy accepted his unexpected sentence with a remarkably calm and peaceful mind.
He knew that his ambitious new life of honest labor would simply have to wait until he was released from custody.
Sitting quietly in the transport wagon, he realized that the cold winter would no longer trouble him inside the comfortable prison walls.
As the heavy iron gates closed behind him, he felt that everything had happened for a reason, and his long journey of change had finally begun.
